No, the conviction should not be reversed. Causation is satisfied because the defective drug hastened the patient's death, and a defendant who accelerates a death is a legal cause even when the victim was terminal. Malice is also likely supported, since knowingly shipping a known sub-strength cancer drug to patients who depend on it shows extreme indifference to human life. The strongest argument for reversal is that the record may not show he understood the lethal risk rather than only the financial one, which could support a manslaughter reduction instead.

CONFIDENCE: 70
